name: Crucible Industries Harmonic Zweihander HZ-1 'Earthquake'
description:
A massive two-handed sword that uses a bass-frequency vibration system tuned to transmit kinetic shockwaves through whatever it strikes. The Earthquake does not merely cut — on impact, its blade discharges a low-frequency pulse that propagates through the target material, causing structural fracturing well beyond the point of contact. A strike against a wall does not just damage the impact point; it sends cracks radiating outward in a two-meter radius.

The HZ-1's blade is 120 centimeters of aerogel-reinforced carbon composite, thick enough to absorb its own shockwave without self-destructing. The vibration generator is housed in the massive crossguard and produces a subsonic hum that can be felt rather than heard — a deep bone-level vibration that makes nearby observers instinctively uncomfortable. At full power, the weapon's strikes can fracture reinforced concrete and shatter ballistic glass.

Crucible built the Earthquake as a siege weapon for corporate breach teams that needed to break through hardened barriers without explosives. The weapon requires significant physical strength or powered augmentation to wield effectively — at 5.2 kilograms, it is one of the heaviest melee weapons in active service. Users tend to be either heavily augmented operators or naturally large individuals who have built their entire fighting style around the weapon's ponderous but devastating delivery.
specifications:
blade_length: 120 cm
total_length: 168 cm
weight: 5.2 kg
vibration_frequency: 12 Hz (subsonic)
shockwave_radius: ~2 meters from impact point
power_source: Crossguard-integrated fuel cell, 2 hours active
blade_material: Aerogel-reinforced carbon composite
tactical_use: The Earthquake is a breaching and area-denial weapon. Its shockwave propagation means that every strike damages an area rather than a point, making it effective against barriers, clustered opponents, and structural targets. In melee combat, opponents who block the weapon still receive transmitted shockwave damage through their own weapon or shield. The primary limitation is speed — the weapon is too heavy for rapid exchanges, and each swing requires a full-body commitment that leaves the wielder momentarily vulnerable.
cultural_context: The HZ-1 has become associated with a particular archetype in GLMZ's combat culture: the heavy hitter who sacrifices speed and subtlety for absolute destructive power. Earthquake wielders are both respected and avoided — their presence changes the geometry of any engagement. The weapon's subsonic hum has been sampled by GLMZ's industrial music scene, and the term 'earthquake drop' in music refers to a bass hit that vibrates the listener's chest.
story_hooks: An Earthquake strike caused a structural cascade that collapsed a section of lower-tier housing — killing fourteen people who were not involved in the fight. The wielder claims it was a weapon malfunction; engineering analysis suggests the weapon performed exactly as designed.
A miniaturized version of the shockwave generator has appeared in the black market, small enough to be integrated into a standard-sized weapon. The technology has leaked from Crucible.
related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Resonance Hammer RH-3 'Earthquake'

physical_description.visual_profile: An imposing two-handed sword with a distinctly oversized, anvil-like presence. The blade is noticeably thick and blocky rather than tapered, with a pronounced aerodynamic form optimized for shockwave transmission rather than slicing. The crossguard is dramatically enlarged—a complex engineering assembly housing the vibration generator—giving the weapon a top-heavy, intentional brutality. Silhouette reads as siege equipment first, sword second.
physical_description.dimensions: Total length: 168 cm. Blade length: 120 cm (unusually thick, approximately 8 cm wide at spine). Crossguard spans 22 cm across. Grip section: 46 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and deliberate—5.2 kg feels distributed through the entire length, making it neither point-heavy nor handle-heavy, but requiring full-body leverage. Unwieldy for speed, but balanced for sustained power delivery.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerogel-reinforced carbon composite blade; reinforced steel/titanium alloy frame and crossguard; industrial-grade polymer grip wrapping.
physical_description.finish: Matte dark gunmetal with brushed steel accents on the crossguard. The blade surface is slightly textured—micro-etched to reduce reflection and show the layered composite structure beneath. Battle-worn in typical field condition: hairline cracks visible in the composite, scuff marks from barrier contact, minor corrosion staining around the crossguard seams.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary; brushed steel silver crossguard; deep charcoal polymer grip. Faint iridescent shimmer in the aerogel layers visible under side-light, suggesting internal structural complexity.
physical_description.grip_texture: Deeply textured polymer with raised geometric channels—non-slip even when wet or bloodied. Wrapped in reinforced synthetic cord at the base for additional grip security during full-force swings.
distinctive_features: Massive, over-engineered crossguard housing visible vibration generator casing with cooling vents
Faint hairline resonance marks etched into the blade surface—stress fracture patterns that show the material has absorbed repeated shockwave discharge
Subtle LED indicator strip (amber/red) running along the crossguard spine showing fuel cell status and vibration frequency output
Deep pitting along the blade edges from impact with concrete and reinforced barriers
Micro-vent array across the pommel for heat dissipation from the integrated fuel cell
Asymmetrical weight distribution markers (material variation lines) showing internal aerogel reinforcement pattern
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: "CRUCIBLE INDUSTRIES" stamped in bold sans-serif across the crossguard face. Smaller "HZ-1 EARTHQUAKE" designation below. Serial number engraved into the tang near the grip (alphanumeric, cyberpunk aesthetic). "BREACH CLASSIFIED — TIER 4+ AUTHORIZATION" warning stamp in red on one side of the blade near the crossguard. Manufacturing date code pressed into the pommel base.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but visibly duty-worn. The blade shows strategic pitting and impact scarring concentrated on the striking edge, indicating regular deployment against structural targets. The crossguard housing shows scuff marks and minor dent scarring from rough handling and barrier contact. The polymer grip shows compression wear from sustained gripping during full-power swings. Overall impression: a weapon that has broken through real barriers, not a showpiece.
